title: Adopt NSA 5G Architecture for Phase 2 Core Network Rollout
description: The Architecture Review Board approved a Non-Standalone 5G architecture for Phase 2, leveraging the existing 4G LTE core as an anchor network. The decision was driven by faster time-to-market projections and lower immediate CapEx compared to a full SA deployment.
rationale: Initial modelling showed NSA deployment would reduce Phase 2 CapEx by approximately 28% and accelerate commercial launch by 6 months. Three board members flagged SA as the long-term standard but were overruled on cost grounds. No independent vendor-neutral analysis was commissioned before ratification.
alternatives_considered: Full Standalone (SA) 5G core with Nokia AirScale — higher CapEx but future-proof; rejected due to 9-month lead time.
Hybrid NSA-SA dual-stack with phased migration — medium complexity; rejected because the vendor quoted a 22% premium.
Defer Phase 2 by 12 months to allow SA ecosystem maturity — rejected by CTO as commercially unacceptable.
root_cause_analysis: Post-implementation review identified three compounding failures: (1) The cost model excluded hidden integration costs for the billing mediation layer, adding ₹4.2 crore to the NSA path. (2) The architecture team did not consult Network Operations who had direct experience with NSA anchor failures in the Phase 1 pilot. (3) The decision was rushed to meet a board presentation deadline, bypassing the standard 2-week independent review cycle. These failures led to a technically inferior architecture that blocked the Pune pilot and forced a re-architecture exercise estimated at 3 months of additional engineering effort.

title: Implement Activity-Based Costing Model for Network OpEx
description: Decision made by the leadership team regarding implement activity-based costing model for network opex. This decision was taken after a structured evaluation of available options and was ratified at the Architecture Review Board meeting.
rationale: At the time of the decision, the selected option appeared to offer the best balance of cost, speed, and risk. However, subsequent implementation revealed significant constraints that were not adequately captured in the options analysis. The decision was taken under time pressure without sufficient cross-functional review, which contributed to the negative outcome documented in the root cause analysis.
alternatives_considered: Option A: Open-source stack — rejected due to higher CapEx and longer implementation lead time.
Option B: Co-sourced delivery model — rejected due to vendor lock-in risk and limited local support.
Option C: Accelerated rollout — rejected because it did not meet the 12-month delivery commitment.
Option D: Status quo retention — rejected as it defers critical risk without resolution.
Option E: Phased hybrid approach — rejected due to integration complexity exceeding team capacity.
root_cause_analysis: Post-decision review confirmed that the chosen approach introduced a vendor dependency that was not adequately assessed during the options analysis. Key risk factors that were underweighted included: (1) single-vendor sourcing for a mission-critical component, (2) absence of contractual SLAs for escalation paths, and (3) no contingency plan if the vendor failed to meet integration milestones. The architecture team lacked direct experience with the chosen platform, which compounded delivery risk.
